own_solution.law: lambda = hc / sqrt(2 mc^2 K) (non-relativistic de Broglie)

notes: Agrees with pass 1 (pass 1 reported in nm; the target unit is pm, 0.16692 nm = 166.92 pm). Checked certified answers: K = 104 eV gives sqrt(106,288,000) = 10309.61 eV, lambda = 120.276 pm; K = 154 eV gives 98.841 pm; K = 254 eV gives sqrt(259,588,000) = 16111.74 eV, lambda = 76.963 pm. All match. Largest K (254 eV) is negligible relative to 511 keV, so the non-relativistic relation holds; the wiring's 'at most 500 eV' bound is true though loose. The D sentences give the energy to a different body with no physical path to this electron. Minimal pairs T70DC/T6C4C and T8B18/TB699 state the same 100 eV and differ only in the recipient. The assumption mentioning 'every photon energy' is irrelevant boilerplate (no photon in the item) but harmless.
